response: No, clinical predictors are not always adequate to rule out cervical spine fractures in geriatric blunt trauma patients with low-energy mechanisms. Advanced age, even with low-energy trauma, increases the risk of cervical spine injury due to decreased bone density and other age-related changes. Therefore, a high index of suspicion and liberal use of imaging studies, such as CT scans, are often necessary to evaluate the cervical spine in this population. Relying solely on clinical predictors may lead to missed diagnoses, as geriatric patients may not always exhibit typical symptoms or signs of cervical spine injury.
